title: Being conscious adds little utility to a mental state

statements.text: Unlike metacognition, which has clear benefit, a mental state being conscious probably adds little if any utility beyond what the state does when it is not conscious. Rationality, planning and executive control run on intentional content, and conveying thoughts to others needs only expressing them, not reporting them.

sources.quote: it is unlikely that there is much, if any, utility to mental states’ being conscious over and above the utility those states have when they are not conscious
Rationality and inference depend entirely on rational connections among the contents of cognitive and volitional states
Consciousness is not needed for the social utility of letting others know about our thoughts.
